agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager gets the gaps up front, a concrete plan to close them, and a credible safety-training parallel, so a phone screen is likely, though nothing yet shows the writer knows how a regulated plant works.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief, and the letter rightly declines the unsupported 'cut training in half' promise; the only stretch is the lead-in 'what the people I've trained have done,' which also covers students' exam results.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives the seven years and the 17-point gain, but leaves stronger true forms unused: roughly 1,000 student-years in labs without a serious injury, about 18 new teachers trained, and a 41% relative rise in the pass rate.

right_comparison.reason: The AP result is set correctly against her own first-year baseline, and the new-teacher training is fairly compared to a new hire working alone, but the safety record has no before-2019 comparison and the brief gives none.

qualification.reason: The GMP course 'before my start date' and the 90-day review are checkable dates, but the shortening plan has no number and nothing says what happens if the target is missed.

objections.reason: It meets the main objection head-on by naming the regulated-industry, GMP-records and LMS gaps with specific fixes, and it raises no objection the brief already answers.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter in the requested form; it leaves out the user's requested halving claim, which is honest but departs from the brief.
